verses.text: For the music director, to the tune of “Do Not Destroy.” A poem by David. Do you who stay silent really speak for what is right? Do you people judge fairly?
Deep down you plan injustice. With your hands you deal out violence across the land.
The wicked stray from the womb. From birth they go their own way, spreading lies.
Their venom is like a snake’s, like a deaf cobra that closes its ears,
refusing to hear the snake charmers, however skillfully they play.
God, break the teeth in their mouths. LORD, knock out the fangs of those young lions.
Let them disappear like water running off. When they draw their bows, let their arrows lose their points.
Let them disappear like a snail that melts away, like a stillborn child who never saw the sun.
Before your pots feel the heat of the thorns, he’ll sweep away both the green branches and the burning ones.
Those who do right will rejoice when they see justice done. They’ll wash their feet in the blood of the wicked,
and people will say, “There really is a reward for the righteous. There really is a God who judges the earth.”
